notes: Direct HTTP fetch (tier 1) + Playwright (tier 2) to render the client-side Unbxd product counts. No bot protection, no Claude-specific robots.txt disallow. Found and closely investigated a candidate: the top nav has a department-tier tab (id='dept-sale') whose CUSTOMER-FACING label is the generic word 'Sale', linking to /in/en/sis/clearancesale. The URL's internal CMS slug ('clearancesale') and its Google-Analytics promotion tracking ids (e.g. 'SISpage_ClearanceSale_shopbycategory', 'SISpage_ClearanceSale_homewaredeals') do use the word 'clearance', so this page was opened and its child widgets inspected in full: it is a landing page of ~14 banner tiles, each linking to an ordinary category page filtered by a discount-percentage query param (not a distinct clearance-branded page) - e.g. /in/en/c/bedroom-wardrobes?discount=20,100 (31 products), /in/en/c/bedroom-beds?discount=40,100 (88), /in/en/c/livingroom-sofas?discount=50,100 (99), /in/en/c/livingroom-tables?discount=50,100 (64), /in/en/c/diningroom-diningtablesets?discount=20,100 (14), /in/en/c/kitchen-storageandcontainers?discount=20,100 (88), /in/en/c/dining-crockery?discount=20,100 (269), /in/en/c/bathandlaundry?discount=20,100 (270), /in/en/c/furnishing-bedding?discount=20,100 (1177), /in/en/c/decor-garden?discount=20,100 (221), /in/en/c/decor-lighting?discount=20,100 (1290), /in/en/c/furniture?discount=20,100 (865, a whole-department view overlapping the more specific furniture rows above), /in/en/c/decor?discount=20,100 (2765, a whole-department view), and /in/en/c/livingroom-tvandmediaunits?q=:index:price (34, sorted by price with no discount filter at all). Each count is exact (site's own numberOfProducts in the SSR/rendered search-index JSON). EXCLUDED all of these from Clearance rows because, per the brief's Sale-vs-Clearance test, the word 'Clearance' never once appears anywhere the customer can actually see: not in the top-nav label (which reads 'Sale'), not in any on-page heading/breadcrumb of the landing page itself (no <h1>, no visible section title uses the word), and not in any of the 14 destination category pages (each is the ordinary category page, e.g. meta title 'Buy Wooden Wardrobes Online...', just with a discount facet pre-applied via URL param - an arbitrary/temporary promotional filter, not the site's own permanent clearance/outlet taxonomy). The scale of some counts (2765 products at >=20% off for the entire Decor department, 1290 for all of Decor-Lighting) is far more consistent with routine seasonal/promotional discounting than genuine end-of-line/outlet stock. This company's own prior Home-Decor extraction pass (see notes/243.md) already documented this exact storefront having 'a legacy/orphaned parallel taxonomy...tagged onto products but not linked from any live navigation', so a legacy-sounding internal URL slug that the customer never sees is treated as the same kind of artifact here, not as genuine current taxonomy. Sitewide text search confirmed zero hits for 'outlet', 'final sale', 'last chance', 'end of line', 'discontinued' anywhere in the rendered homepage. Sitemaps (decor/livingroom/kitchen/bedroom/diningroom/toppages.xml) grepped for clearance/outlet/final-sale/last-chance/end-of-line slugs - 0 hits (remaining department sitemaps hit HTTP 429 rate-limiting on /sitemap/* and were not retried per the no-backoff-loop rule, but the category-URL naming scheme already sampled never encodes merchandising concepts into slugs, so this is not expected to change the conclusion). Conclusion: no genuine Clearance/Outlet PLP exists on this storefront under the brief's definition; the closest candidate is a generic, internally-legacy-named 'Sale' hub that was investigated in full and excluded.
